title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA1RF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA1RF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves three passes over the regular parts of the tape and the halting situation (kernel), and no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in 109 steps.

What it does. The head sweeps the whole tape. At the left-end turns the tape is 0 0, a few copies of 110, then a run qa of the 24-cell word q = 010110101101010110101101, a run sb of s = 101010110110110, runs of 10 whose lengths roughly double (5, 16, 38, 78, 157 at step 7,087,597), a run of 101110110110, and an irregular right end. The q-run gains a copy every few round trips while the material to its right is consumed; when it runs out the regions are rebuilt and q starts again from a few copies.
Where a halt would come from. Only D reading a 1 halts, and D is entered only from C reading a 0; so C>0 1 halts (halt_C). In the run D always reads a 0.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 42,923 cells have been visited and 28,048 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.539). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.379).

claims.title: Every way to a halt
claims.text: Two steps before any halt the machine is in B>0 0 1; no other configuration halts within three steps.

claims.title: Three passes
claims.text: A moving right rewrites each copy of q (in the rotation 011010110101011010110101) as 100111001111100111001111, 32 steps a copy; C moving left rewrites the result back to q, 68 steps a copy; A moving right turns each 011 into 100. All for any number of copies.

claims.title: The halting situation
claims.text: C>0 1 halts after two steps; D is entered only from C reading a 0.

claims.title: Growth and rebuilding
claims.text: At the left-end turns the q-run grows from 3 copies (561,704 steps) to 111 (4,263,440) while the s-run shrinks from 50 copies to 7; by 4.7·106 both are gone. Then q starts again (10 copies at 5.19·106), an s-run of 36 copies reappears at 5.9·106 and stays at 35 or 36 up to 1.2·107 steps while q grows to 109 and the region of 101110110110 further right shrinks.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The next step is the exact rule of one round trip on the sequence of regions: which region feeds which, and how the rebuild happens.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1RF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD1RF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB1LF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. This machine lines up several periodic patterns on its tape and slowly turns one into another, like a counter with very long digits. This page runs it in your browser.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 42,923 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Regions that feed each other
html: Stop the simulator at the turns at the left end and write c = 110, q = 010110101101010110101101 (24 cells) and s = 101010110110110 (15 cells). At step 7,087,597 the tape starts
B>c2 0 c2 1 0 c 1 0 c 1 q40 0 1 0 c 1 0 c 1 0 1 0 c 1 0 1 0 1 0 c2 1 0 c 1 0 s36 1 0 c6 1 0 s c (10)5 s c (10)16 s c (10)38 c 1 0 c (10)78 c2 0 c2 (10)157 ...

and continues with a long run of 101110110110, and an irregular stretch at the right end. So the tape is a row of periodic regions with short joints between them; the runs of 10 have lengths 5, 16, 38, 78, 157, roughly doubling, as if each held one level of a counter.

Counting copies at the left-end turns shows how they feed each other. The q-run grows from 3 copies (step 561,704) to 111 (step 4,263,440) while the s-run shrinks from 50 copies to 7; by step 4.7·106 both are gone and the q-run starts again from a few copies. After that an s-run of 36 copies sits still while q grows again and the region further right shrinks. It looks like a counter whose digits are whole regions.

The passes are fast rewrites one copy at a time. Moving right, A rewrites each copy of q as 100111001111100111001111 in 32 steps; moving left, C restores it in 68 steps. For example A>011 011 011 becomes 100 100 100 A> in 15 steps (pass_right_c).

The only halt is C>0 1 (halt_C): C writes a 1 and steps right onto a 1 in state D, which has no transition for 1. Finding the exact round-trip rule of the regions, and an invariant from it that keeps D off a 1, is the open step.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.539). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.379).
After 109 steps the tape spans 42,923 cells (27,961 left of the start, 4,780 right), with a density of 1s of 0.653.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1RF: rename A→E, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→F; it is this table started in state B
  • 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD1RF: rename A→D, B→E, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→F; it is this table started in state C
  • 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB1LF: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→A, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state E, in a mirror

family: two-sided bouncer with several periodic regions (hierarchical counter)
summary: Full sweeps over a tape made of several periodic regions in a row (a 24-cell word q, a 15-cell word s, runs of 10, a 12-cell word); the q-region grows while a region further right is used up, then the pattern is rebuilt, like a counter with long digits. Open.
